description: Shared update policy for JanWelker's repositories. See README.md.

lockFileMaintenance.description: Refreshes every transitive package at once and has no release timestamp to age, so it opens on Mondays, a whole-day window Renovate cannot miss, and merges on green required checks like any patch.

packageRules.description: Everything below a major merges on its own once the required checks are green.
A major opens at 19:00 Zurich time and waits for a human to merge it.
Below 1.0 a minor is the breaking release, so it waits for a human like a major.

These registries publish no release timestamps, so a required timestamp would hold their updates forever and no age can be enforced; they skip the release age altogether, which also keeps the dashboard free of the timestamp-optional warnings, and third-party images there wait for a human instead. Without an age there is no renovate/stability-days status, so not-pending would hold the PR for prNotPendingHours, restarted by every rebase; open it at once.

A digest update from a trusted publisher is a rebuild of a tag already accepted, mostly base-package security fixes; it merges on green required checks like any digest instead of waiting for a human. A new tag from them still waits.

Our own images: no release age to wait out, so no renovate/stability-days status either. With CI on the PR only, the branch then has no status at all, and not-pending would hold the PR for prNotPendingHours, restarted by every new release; open it at once and let the required checks gate the merge.
Our own reusable workflows and presets: no release age to wait out.
TypeScript stays on 6.x everywhere: 7 is the native Go port, and the Svelte and typescript-eslint toolchains do not support it yet.
